exposure: CS indications (e.g., repeated CS, primary sections, CPD, failure to progress, multiple foetuses, malpresentation, scar rupture, pre-eclampsia, late pregnancy bleeding, non-reassuring fetal heart rate (NRFHR), maternal request)
cohort: The study included 3,385 women who had Cesarean sections in 2008 and 2018 at Salmaniya Medical Complex in Bahrain.
finding: The increased rate of Cesarean sections was found to be justified by a significant increase in non-reassuring fetal heart rate (NRFHR) and maternal request, occurring more predominantly in non-Bahraini populations.
mod_finding: The overall Cesarean section rate increased from 22.4% in 2008 to 32.8% in 2018, with a significant rise in non-reassuring fetal heart rate (NRFHR) as an indication for this mode of birth, and varied by nationality.
